title: Die ungleichen Kinder Evas
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 180. Text from Wikisource (twice proofread against the original). 1857 spelling preserved (daß, mußte, häßlich, Noth).
about: An etiological tale set just after the expulsion from Paradise: Eve hides her plainer children when God comes to visit and presents only the handsome ones, so God assigns each a station in life — king down to farmhand — and then, once he sees through the trick, does the same for the ones she tried to hide. It reads as an explanation for why people’s stations differ rather than a story with a hero, and Eve’s closing exchange with God carries the tale’s real point.

sentences.t: Als Adam und Eva aus dem Paradies vertrieben waren, so mußten sie auf unfruchtbarer Erde sich ein Haus bauen und im Schweiße ihres Angesichts ihr Brot essen.
sentences.l: When Adam and Eve had been driven out of Paradise, they had to build themselves a house on unfruitful earth and eat their bread in the sweat of their countenance.
sentences.i: When Adam and Eve had been driven out of Paradise, they had to build themselves a house on barren ground and eat their bread in the sweat of their brow.
sentences.n: so after the opening clause simply resumes the main sentence; German keeps it where English drops it. im Schweiße ihres Angesichts is the wording of Genesis 3:19 — das Angesicht is the face, countenance, here in the genitive (the shared entry for angesichts was written for the preposition ‘in the sight of’, a different word).

sentences.t: Adam hackte das Feld und Eva spann Wolle.
sentences.l: Adam hoed the field and Eve spun wool.
sentences.n: Wolle is wool, the noun; the shared entry for wolle was written for the verb wollen. The two labours divide the household in the old way — the man to the field, the woman to the distaff.

sentences.t: Eva brachte jedes Jahr ein Kind zur Welt, die Kinder waren aber ungleich, einige schön, andere häßlich.
sentences.l: Eve brought a child into the world every year, but the children were unequal, some beautiful, others ugly.
sentences.i: Every year Eve bore a child, but the children were not alike: some beautiful, others ugly.
sentences.n: zur Welt bringen — to bring into the world, to bear. ungleich, ‘unlike, unequal’, is the word of the title and carries both senses at once.

sentences.t: Nachdem eine geraume Zeit verlaufen war, sendete Gott einen Engel an die beiden und ließ ihnen entbieten daß er kommen und ihren Haushalt schauen wollte.
sentences.l: After a good while had run by, God sent an angel to the two and had it announced to them that he wanted to come and look at their household.
sentences.i: When a good while had gone by, God sent an angel to the pair and had word sent them that he meant to come and see their household.
sentences.n: eine geraume Zeit — a considerable while. entbieten is an old formal verb for sending word; ließ ihnen entbieten = had word conveyed to them.

sentences.t: Eva, freudig daß der Herr so gnädig war, säuberte emsig ihr Haus, schmückte es mit Blumen und streute Binsen auf den Estrich.
sentences.l: Eve, joyful that the Lord was so gracious, busily cleaned her house, decked it with flowers and strewed rushes on the floor.
sentences.i: Eve, glad that the Lord was so gracious, cleaned her house busily, decked it with flowers, and strewed rushes over the floor.
sentences.n: der Estrich is the floor of a house — beaten clay, plaster or stone — and is plain High German here, not the Low German form the shared entry describes. Strewing fresh rushes was the old way of making a room fit for a guest.

sentences.t: Dann holte sie ihre Kinder herbei, aber nur die schönen.
sentences.l: Then she fetched her children here, but only the beautiful ones.
sentences.i: Then she brought her children out — but only the beautiful ones.
sentences.n: herbei holen is separable: to fetch to where one is. Everything in the tale follows from the aber nur.

sentences.t: Sie wusch und badete sie, kämmte ihnen die Haare, legte ihnen neugewaschene Hemder an und ermahnte sie in der Gegenwart des Herrn sich anständig und züchtig zu betragen.
sentences.l: She washed and bathed them, combed them the hair, put newly washed shirts on them and admonished them to conduct themselves decently and modestly in the presence of the Lord.
sentences.i: She washed and bathed them, combed their hair, put newly washed shirts on them, and charged them to behave decently and modestly in the Lord’s presence.
sentences.n: kämmte ihnen die Haare is the dative of possession: German says ‘combed the hair to them’ where English says ‘their hair’. Hemder is the older plural of Hemd (modern Hemden); anziehen is separable — legte … an.

sentences.t: Sie sollten sich vor ihm sittig neigen, die Hand darbieten und auf seine Fragen bescheiden und verständig antworten.
sentences.l: They should bow decorously before him, offer the hand and answer his questions modestly and sensibly.
sentences.i: They were to bow decorously before him, hold out their hand, and answer his questions modestly and sensibly.
sentences.n: sollten reports Eve’s instruction — they were to do so. darbieten is separable (dar + bieten), to offer, hold out; the prefix dar is High German here, not the Low German word for ‘there’ that the shared entry gives.

sentences.t: Die häßlichen Kinder aber sollten sich nicht sehen lassen.
sentences.l: The ugly children, however, were not to let themselves be seen.
sentences.i: The ugly children, though, were not to show themselves at all.
sentences.n: sich sehen lassen — to let oneself be seen, to show oneself. häßlich is the 1857 spelling of hässlich.

sentences.t: Das eine verbarg sie unter das Heu, das andere unter das Dach, das dritte in das Stroh, das vierte in den Ofen, das fünfte in den Keller, das sechste unter eine Kufe, das siebente unter das Weinfaß, das achte unter ihren alten Pelz, das neunte und zehnte unter das Tuch, aus dem sie ihnen Kleider zu machen pflegte, und das elfte und zwölfte unter das Leder, aus dem sie ihnen die Schuhe zuschnitt.
sentences.l: The one she hid under the hay, the other under the roof, the third in the straw, the fourth in the oven, the fifth in the cellar, the sixth under a tub, the seventh under the wine-cask, the eighth under her old fur, the ninth and tenth under the cloth out of which she used to make them clothes, and the eleventh and twelfth under the leather out of which she cut their shoes.
sentences.i: One she hid under the hay, another under the roof, the third in the straw, the fourth in the oven, the fifth in the cellar, the sixth under a tub, the seventh under the wine-cask, the eighth under her old fur, the ninth and tenth under the cloth she used for making their clothes, and the eleventh and twelfth under the leather she cut their shoes from.
sentences.n: Twelve hiding-places, counted off in order, all of them the ordinary stuff of a poor household; the order of the counting is the order in which these twelve are blessed later. pflegte with a zu-infinitive is ‘used to’ — a different verb from pflegen, to tend; zuschneiden, to cut out to shape, is separable.

sentences.t: Eben war sie fertig geworden, als es an die Hausthüre klopfte.
sentences.l: Just then she had got finished when there was a knocking at the house-door.
sentences.i: She had only just finished when there came a knock at the house door.
sentences.n: es klopfte is impersonal — ‘it knocked’, there was a knocking. Hausthüre keeps the 1857 th- and the old final -e (modern Haustür).

sentences.t: Adam blickte durch eine Spalte und sah daß es der Herr war.
sentences.l: Adam looked through a crack and saw that it was the Lord.
sentences.n: durch eine Spalte — through a chink in the door; they look out before opening, as at any unexpected visit.

sentences.t: Ehrerbietig öffnete er und der himmlische Vater trat ein.
sentences.l: Reverently he opened, and the heavenly Father stepped in.
sentences.i: He opened reverently, and the heavenly Father came in.
sentences.n: eintreten is separable: trat … ein. Ehrerbietig stands first, so the verb takes second place and the subject follows it.

sentences.t: Da standen die schönen Kinder in der Reihe, neigten sich, boten ihm die Hände dar und knieten nieder.
sentences.l: There stood the beautiful children in the row, bowed themselves, offered him the hands and knelt down.
sentences.i: There the beautiful children stood in a row, bowed, held out their hands to him, and knelt down.
sentences.n: boten … dar is the past of darbieten, with the prefix dar waiting at the end of the clause — the shared entries for both boten and dar were written for other words. nieder knien works the same way: knieten … nieder.

sentences.t: Der Herr aber fieng an sie zu segnen, legte auf den ersten seine Hände und sprach „du sollst ein gewaltiger König werden:“
sentences.l: But the Lord began to bless them, laid his hands on the first and spoke “you shall become a mighty king:”
sentences.i: But the Lord set about blessing them, laid his hands on the first, and said, “You shall become a mighty king:”
sentences.n: anfangen is separable — fieng … an, with the 1857 -ie- for fing. The colon inside the closing quotation mark is how the 1857 text runs one speech straight on into the next.

sentences.t: ebenso zu dem zweiten „du ein Fürst:“
sentences.l: likewise to the second “you [shall become] a prince:”
sentences.i: and so to the second, “you a prince:”
sentences.n: The verb is gapped all down the list: du [sollst ein] Fürst [werden], understood from the first blessing and supplied here in square brackets.

sentences.t: zu dem dritten „du ein Graf:“
sentences.l: to the third “you a count:”
sentences.n: ein Graf is a count, the rank below a prince; the list is descending through the estates in order of standing.

sentences.t: zu dem vierten „du ein Ritter:“
sentences.l: to the fourth “you a knight:”
sentences.n: der Ritter, the knight — the estate that holds land in return for service in arms.

sentences.t: zu dem fünften „du ein Edelmann:“
sentences.l: to the fifth “you a nobleman:”
sentences.n: Edelmann is literally ‘noble man’: a man of gentle birth without a title of rank.

sentences.t: zu dem sechsten „du ein Bürger:“
sentences.l: to the sixth “you a townsman:”
sentences.n: der Bürger is a burgher, a man with the freedom of a town; with him the list leaves the nobility behind.

sentences.t: zum siebenten „du ein Kaufmann:“
sentences.l: to the seventh “you a merchant:”
sentences.n: zum = zu dem. siebente is the older form of siebte; der Kaufmann trades rather than makes.

sentences.t: zu dem achten „du ein gelehrter Mann.“
sentences.l: to the eighth “you a learned man.”
sentences.n: ein gelehrter Mann — a learned man, a scholar; the full stop closes the first blessing. The shared entries for achte and achten were written for the verb achten, to heed; here both are simply the ordinal ‘eighth’.

sentences.t: Er ertheilte ihnen also allen seinen reichen Segen.
sentences.l: He imparted thus to them all his rich blessing.
sentences.i: So he gave them all his rich blessing.
sentences.n: ertheilen (1857 spelling of erteilen) is the formal verb for bestowing a blessing, advice or permission. also is ‘thus’, never the English ‘also’.

sentences.t: Als Eva sah daß der Herr so mild und gnädig war, dachte sie „ich will meine ungestalten Kinder herbeiholen, vielleicht daß er ihnen auch seinen Segen gibt.“
sentences.l: When Eve saw that the Lord was so mild and gracious, she thought “I will fetch my misshapen children here, perhaps that he gives them his blessing too.”
sentences.i: When Eve saw how mild and gracious the Lord was, she thought, “I will fetch my misshapen children out; perhaps he will give them his blessing too.”
sentences.n: ungestalt is an old word for misshapen, ill-formed. vielleicht daß … is an older turn: ‘perhaps [it may be] that …’.

sentences.t: Sie lief also und holte sie aus dem Heu, Stroh, Ofen, und wo sie sonst hin versteckt waren, hervor.
sentences.l: So she ran and fetched them out of the hay, straw, oven, and wherever else they were hidden away, forth.
sentences.i: So she ran and brought them out — out of the hay, the straw, the oven, and wherever else they had been hidden.
sentences.n: hervor holen is separable, and the prefix hervor waits to the very end of a long sentence: holte … hervor. wo … hin is split in the same way: where they had been hidden to.

sentences.t: Da kam die ganze grobe, schmutzige, grindige und rußige Schaar.
sentences.l: Then came the whole coarse, dirty, scabby and sooty troop.
sentences.i: Then in came the whole coarse, dirty, scabby, sooty crew.
sentences.n: grindig means scabby, crusted with sores; the 1857 text does not soften the description of the hidden children. Schaar is the 1857 spelling of Schar, a band or troop.

sentences.t: Der Herr lächelte, betrachtete sie alle und sprach „auch diese will ich segnen.“
sentences.l: The Lord smiled, looked them all over and spoke “these too I will bless.”
sentences.i: The Lord smiled, looked them all over, and said, “These too I will bless.”
sentences.n: auch diese stands first for weight, with the verb second: these as well.

sentences.t: Er legte auf den ersten die Hände und sprach zu ihm „du sollst werden ein Bauer,“
sentences.l: He laid his hands on the first and spoke to him “you shall become a farmer,”
sentences.i: He laid his hands on the first and said to him, “You shall become a farmer,”
sentences.n: du sollst werden ein Bauer puts the infinitive before the noun — a solemn older word order; ordinary German would be du sollst ein Bauer werden. der Bauer is the peasant who works the land with his own hands.

sentences.t: zu dem zweiten „du ein Fischer,“
sentences.l: to the second “you [shall become] a fisherman,”
sentences.i: to the second, “you a fisherman,”
sentences.n: The verb is gapped from the first blessing of this second list and is supplied here in square brackets. Fischer is plain High German here, a fisherman; the shared entry’s Low German label belongs to another tale.

sentences.t: zu dem dritten „du ein Schmied,“
sentences.l: to the third “you a smith,”
sentences.n: der Schmied, the smith, who works iron at the forge.

sentences.t: zu dem vierten „du ein Lohgerber,“
sentences.l: to the fourth “you a tanner,”
sentences.n: der Lohgerber is a bark-tanner: die Lohe is the ground oak-bark whose liquor tans the hide. The exact 1857 range of these trade-names is not always sharp — Lohgerber is one of several tanning trades, distinguished from the white-tanner who used alum.

sentences.t: zu dem fünften „du ein Weber,“
sentences.l: to the fifth “you a weaver,”
sentences.n: der Weber, the weaver, who works cloth on a loom — in 1857 still very often a trade carried on at home.

sentences.t: zu dem sechsten „du ein Schuhmacher,“
sentences.l: to the sixth “you a shoemaker,”
sentences.n: der Schuhmacher, the shoemaker — der Schuh, shoe, and machen, to make: the trade that turns the tanner’s leather into shoes.

sentences.t: zu dem siebenten „du ein Schneider,“
sentences.l: to the seventh “you a tailor,”
sentences.n: der Schneider, the tailor, from schneiden, to cut.

sentences.t: zu dem achten „du ein Töpfer,“
sentences.l: to the eighth “you a potter,”
sentences.n: der Töpfer, the potter, from der Topf, pot.

sentences.t: zu dem neunten „du ein Karrenführer,“
sentences.l: to the ninth “you a carter,”
sentences.n: der Karrenführer drives a cart for hire (Karren, cart + führen, to lead, drive).

sentences.t: zu dem zehnten „du ein Schiffer,“
sentences.l: to the tenth “you a boatman,”
sentences.n: der Schiffer is a boatman or skipper on river or lake, a man with his own craft rather than a hired hand.

sentences.t: zu dem elften „du ein Bote,“
sentences.l: to the eleventh “you a messenger,”
sentences.n: der Bote carries letters and errands on foot; the eleventh estate has no craft of its own at all.

sentences.t: zu dem zwölften „du ein Hausknecht dein Lebelang.“
sentences.l: to the twelfth “you a house-servant your whole life long.”
sentences.i: to the twelfth, “you a house-servant all your life long.”
sentences.n: der Hausknecht is a household drudge or ostler, the bottom of the list, and dein Lebelang — all your life long — is added to this one blessing alone. The 1857 text lets the ranking stand without comment; it is the tale’s own account of how the estates came to be.

sentences.t: Als Eva das alles mit angehört hatte, sagte sie „Herr, wie theilst du deinen Segen so ungleich!
sentences.l: When Eve had listened to all that, she said “Lord, how unequally you divide your blessing!
sentences.i: When Eve had listened to all this, she said, “Lord, how unequally you deal out your blessing!
sentences.n: mit anhören — to listen to something one is standing by for; the particle mit is separated from the verb. theilst is the 1857 spelling of teilst (theilen/teilen, to divide).

sentences.t: Es sind doch alle meine Kinder, die ich geboren habe:
sentences.l: They are, after all, all my children whom I have borne:
sentences.i: They are every one of them my children, whom I bore:
sentences.n: Es sind is the impersonal opening German uses where English says ‘they are’. doch is the particle of protest: surely, after all.

sentences.t: deine Gnade sollte über alle gleich ergehen.“
sentences.l: your grace should go forth over all alike.”
sentences.i: your grace should come upon them all alike.”
sentences.n: über jemanden ergehen — to go forth over, to come upon someone; the shared entry for ergehen gives only the idiom Gnade für Recht ergehen lassen, which is a different use.

sentences.t: Gott aber erwiederte „Eva, das verstehst du nicht.
sentences.l: But God replied “Eve, that you do not understand.
sentences.i: But God replied, “Eve, you do not understand this.
sentences.n: das stands first as the object, so the verb comes second and the subject after it.

sentences.t: Mir gebührt und ist Noth daß ich die ganze Welt mit deinen Kindern versehe:
sentences.l: It behoves me and is needful that I furnish the whole world with your children:
sentences.i: It is my part, and it is needful, that I should stock the whole world with your children:
sentences.n: mir gebührt — it falls to me, it is mine by right; ist Noth (1857 spelling of Not) is an old impersonal ‘is needful’. versehen mit — to supply, furnish with.

sentences.t: wenn sie alle Fürsten und Herrn wären, wer sollte Korn bauen, dreschen, malen und backen?
sentences.l: if they were all princes and lords, who should grow corn, thresh, grind and bake?
sentences.i: if they were all princes and lords, who would grow the corn, thresh it, grind it and bake it?
sentences.n: malen here is the older spelling of mahlen, to grind at the mill — not malen, to paint, which is what the shared entry gives; the four verbs follow the corn from field to loaf. wären is past subjunctive: were they all …

sentences.t: wer schmieden, weben, zimmern, bauen, graben, schneiden und nähen?
sentences.l: who forge, weave, do carpentry, build, dig, cut and sew?
sentences.i: who would forge, weave, do the carpentry, build, dig, cut and sew?
sentences.n: The wer sollte of the sentence before still governs this line — the modal is not repeated. graben is the verb to dig; the shared entry gives the noun der Graben, a ditch.

sentences.t: Jeder soll seinen Stand vertreten, daß einer den andern erhalte und alle ernährt werden wie am Leib die Glieder.“
sentences.l: Each is to represent his estate, so that one sustains the other and all are fed as on the body the limbs.”
sentences.i: Each is to fill his own station, so that one sustains another and all are nourished, as the limbs are on a body.”
sentences.n: der Stand is the estate or station a man is born to — the whole social order the tale has been explaining — not the past of stehen that the shared entry gives. erhalte here means sustain, keep alive, and is subjunctive after daß. The image of body and limbs is Paul’s, 1 Corinthians 12.

sentences.t: Da antwortete Eva „ach, Herr, vergib, ich war zu rasch, daß ich dir einredete.
sentences.l: Then Eve answered “ah, Lord, forgive, I was too quick in that I talked back at you.
sentences.i: Then Eve answered, “Ah, Lord, forgive me; I was too hasty in speaking against you.
sentences.n: vergib is the imperative of vergeben, to forgive. jemandem einreden here is to argue at someone, to talk against them — older than the modern sense ‘to talk someone into something’.

sentences.t: Dein göttlicher Wille geschehe auch an meinen Kindern.“
sentences.l: Your divine will be done on my children too.”
sentences.i: May your divine will be done in my children also.”
sentences.n: geschehe is the old optative subjunctive — let it be done — the same form as Dein Wille geschehe in the Lord’s Prayer, which the line quietly echoes. an meinen Kindern: upon, in the case of my children.

glossary.achte: achte — eighth (ordinal; das achte Kind: the eighth child), not the verb achten
glossary.achten: achte — eighth (ordinal, inflected: zu dem achten, to the eighth), not the verb achten
glossary.angesichts: das Angesicht — face, countenance (gen. sg.; im Schweiße ihres Angesichts), not the preposition angesichts
glossary.boten: bieten — offered, held out (3rd pl. past of darbieten: boten … dar), not der Bote, messenger
glossary.dar: darbieten — to offer, present itself (separable particle dar-, standing at the end)
glossary.dreschen: dreschen — to thresh (infinitive; grain beaten out on the barn floor)
glossary.ergehen: ergehen — to go forth, come upon (über jemanden ergehen: to come upon someone)
glossary.erhalte: erhalten — sustain, keep alive (3rd sg. subjunctive after daß), not ‘receive’ here
glossary.estrich: der Estrich — the floor of a house (beaten clay, plaster or stone); plain High German here
glossary.fischer: der Fischer — fisherman (plain High German here)
glossary.graben: graben — to dig (infinitive), not der Graben, a ditch
glossary.malen: mahlen — to grind (at the mill); the 1857 text spells it malen, which is not malen ‘to paint’
glossary.pflegte: pflegen — used to, was accustomed to (3rd sg. past; pflegte + zu-infinitive), not pflegen ‘to tend, care for’
glossary.stand: der Stand — estate, station in life (seinen Stand vertreten: to fill one’s station), not the past of stehen
glossary.weinfaß: das Weinfaß — wine-cask, wine-barrel (das Faß, cask; 1857 ß)
glossary.wolle: die Wolle — wool (acc. sg.), not a form of wollen
